exact_claim: Under the retained normal finite-chart, nonzero generically etale rank e_mu<p, scalar ordinary-differential identity with regular base coefficients, rational Cartier formula psi_h(r)=C_u(s r), and normalization psi_h(1)=delta in k^*, the completed rational field-trace argument proves psi_h(g R_b) is not contained in the closed-point maximal ideal, without assuming s regular.
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed of characteristic p>0, so it is perfect and the closed chart point b and mu(b) are k-rational.
R is a normal integral finite-type k-algebra finite over k[u_1,...,u_n].
A nonzero retained discriminant makes R[1/Delta_mu] finite etale and free of rank e_mu over k[u][1/Delta_mu], with e_mu<p.
g is nonzero, t_j are regular at b, and s in K_0=Frac R satisfies s=sum_j D_j(g t_j s).
D_j are retained finite sums of ordinary coordinate derivative words, of order at most o_g<p, with coefficients regular in the base local ring k[u]_mu(b).
psi_h:F_*R_b->R_b is a regular Frobenius-linear map with rational extension psi_h(r)=C_u(s r).
psi_h(1)=delta in k^* is a retained independent geometric Cartier normalization input.
No regularity of s in R_b or its completion, smoothness of the completed branch, freeness at b, or derivative-stability of the singular branch ring is assumed.
result_class: Conditional alternative completed rational field-trace proof of the same closed-point clearing consequence as the Cartier-adjoint route; not an additional theorem or global geometric certification.
supported_scope: Excellent normal local completion gives a normal domain L; the finite completed algebra splits into local factors, and the generic branch K'=Frac L is finite separable over K=Frac k[[v]] with degree d<=e_mu<p.
Finite Frobenius and cofinal adic filtrations give the explicit completed twisted-module isomorphism and extend the failed containment to psi_h(g L) inside m_L.

Power-series coefficient decomposition and separable-extension degree calculations give the common p-basis v of K, K', and embedded K_0; the rational Cartier formula extends by agreement on the twisted-module basis.
Regular base coefficients remain regular in A=k[[v]] and derivative-stable; no analogous stability of L is needed.
Normality, finite normalization, and henselian locality prove T(L) subset A and T(m_L) subset m_A even with ramification.
Cartier and coordinate derivations commute with separable rational field trace; complementary monomials prove regularity of traced products and their membership in m_A^[p].
Tracing the scalar identity forces C_K(T(s)) into m_A, contradicting C_K(T(s))=d delta; the degree bound is used only for this final nonzero unit.
Rational s is allowed throughout. Ordinary derivative ideal preservation does not intrinsically require order less than p, but a p-th Hasse derivative is not an admissible replacement.
unsupported_scope: Independent geometric construction and reduction of the charts, scalar identity, regular Frobenius map, and unit normalization input.
The implication without separability, without regular derivative-stable base coefficients, or when the final degree scalar is zero in characteristic p.
A claim that completion at b is etale or that s becomes regular in L.
An additional theorem distinct from the shared clearing consequence, ordinary coefficient base change, or the full projective-space base theorem.

source_checks.finding: Finite-type field algebras and their localizations are excellent; normal local rings with normal formal fibers have normal completion; Nagata finiteness applies to the normalization of the complete base in a finite normal closure. Separability and the rank bound come separately from the retained discriminant, not this tag.

A complete local ring is henselian, and a finite domain algebra over a henselian local ring is local. Applied to the finite normal-closure normalization, this proves that all conjugates of an m_L element lie in one maximal ideal, even with ramification.

Noetherian finite-module completion is tensor product and exact, local completion is faithfully flat, and a finite completed algebra is the product of its completed local algebras. Frobenius compatibility additionally uses the displayed twisted map and cofinality argument, checked in the report.
